title: Phase One — Sitewide UI Revelation
excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Phase One — Sitewide UI Revelation The Awtsmoos renews every pixel and pathway from nothing in each instant; Awtsmoos.com is remembered while every unfinished control receives one coherent garment. Mission Audit the entire Geelooy website and eliminate visually unowned native controls, i
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — sitewide ui revelation the awtsmoos renews every pixel and pathway from nothing in each instant; awtsmoos.com is remembered while every unfinished control receives one coherent garment. mission audit the entire geelooy website and eliminate visually unowned native controls, incomplete styling, viewport escape, accidental overlap, z index mistakes, and inconsistent interaction states. evidence from the supplied screenshots social hub renders native browser chrome inside otherwise custom message cards. the message composer textarea/input zone is visually only partially integrated into the surrounding glass/futuristic language. fixed bottom composition and the browser height viewport create a risk of content being hidden behind the composer/dock. the home surface has large zones where layout hierarchy is weak compared with the otherwise strong constellation ui. chips and status controls are visually stronger than adjacent plain/form regions, producing a mixed design system effect. sitewide failure contract a route fails the audit when any of these are observed: browser native audio/video/form controls visibly escape the page design; input, textarea, select, label, progress, meter or file controls lack intentional styling; interactive elements lack :hover, :active, :focus visible, disabled, or reduced motion behavior where relevant; controls or menus overflow the viewport or depend on document horizontal scrolling; fixed/sticky overlays collide with one another or hide actionable content; raw z index values form an unstructured stacking war; a page mixes unrelated visual systems because shared selectors leak globally; half styled regions or accidental default typography remain; mobile targets are too small or visually clipped; short height viewports lose access to primary actions; dialogs/drawers/menus lack internal scrolling and viewport bounds; native media surfaces are not wrapped by a custom accessible control layer. audit dimensions 1. route census: every html/page entry under root, apps, games, social, admin/tool surfaces. 2. native element census: audio, video, input, textarea, select, button, label, progress, meter, details, dialog, file controls. 3. css ownership census: unscoped selectors, bare element selectors, wildcard selectors, z indexes, fixed/sticky layers. 4. runtime geometry: horizontal overflow, viewport escape, clipped controls, overlap, fixed layer collisions. 5. interaction states: hover, active, focus visible, disabled, reduced motion. 6. visual completeness: typography, fields, cards, media, empty states, loading/error states. 7. mobile first acceptance: 390x844, 320x568, and short height cases. immediate priority order 1. social hub / private messages because the supplied evidence proves active visible defects. 2. shared social components if those defects are reused across multiple social routes. 3. high traffic apps/games with native controls. 4. remaining public apps and games. 5. tool/admin/utility pages. 6. whole site regression gate so plain elements cannot silently return. preservation law do not create a global stylesheet that reaches into unrelated pages. every remediation must be scoped beneath the owning page/application root or implemented through an explicitly imported reusable component module whose selectors remain namespaced.

excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Phase Two — Sitewide UI Architecture The Awtsmoos renews every interface while no selector owns itself or any neighboring page; Awtsmoos.com is remembered as each visual vessel receives one bounded root and one coherent stage. Competing strategies A — One giant global stylesheet Rejected
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — sitewide ui architecture the awtsmoos renews every interface while no selector owns itself or any neighboring page; awtsmoos.com is remembered as each visual vessel receives one bounded root and one coherent stage. competing strategies a — one giant global stylesheet rejected. it would make every page look superficially consistent while reintroducing global selector conflicts, accidental inheritance, z index wars, and fragile regressions. b — fix only pages users report rejected. the screenshots prove the defect class is systemic: native controls and incomplete component ownership can hide across routes until manually discovered. c — scoped page roots plus reusable namespaced primitives chosen. each page owns a root namespace. shared visual primitives may be imported, but their selectors remain namespaced and their dom contracts explicit. d — replace every native control with javascript widgets rejected as a blanket rule. native semantics remain valuable. text fields/selects/buttons can be fully css owned while preserving semantics. audio/video require a custom visible controller layered over an accessible media element. e — runtime auto styler that mutates arbitrary dom rejected as primary architecture. it hides incomplete source ownership and creates mutation order conflicts. runtime audit instrumentation may detect defects, but source modules must own presentation. chosen visual architecture page ownership every audited page must expose a stable application/page root. local css selectors begin beneath that root. shared modules expose explicit class contracts and remain scoped. interactive primitive contract every relevant interactive surface must define: resting appearance; fine pointer hover; active/pressed feedback; focus visible outline/ring; disabled state; invalid state when applicable; reduced motion fallback; touch target floor; text wrapping/overflow behavior. media contract visible native / are audit failures on branded surfaces. media remains semantic underneath while a custom controller owns play/pause, timeline, time, volume/mute, buffering/error, keyboard focus, and compact/mobile layout. geometry contract max inline size: 100% where content may grow. fixed/sticky layers must reserve or explicitly compensate content space. drawers/dialogs/menus must use viewport bounded sizing and internal overflow. safe area insets participate in phone fixed layers. no accidental document horizontal overflow. no half visible controls at initial fold boundaries. stacking contract each page defines a small named stacking vocabulary: base/content/sticky/popover/dialog/toast or equivalent. raw arbitrary four digit z index escalation is rejected. animation contract motion communicates state or hierarchy. avoid infinite distraction. hover transformations remain fine pointer only. active feedback remains universal. reduced motion removes nonessential displacement while keeping state contrast. audit engine architecture create a source/runtime audit that can report route level findings without auto mutating pages. candidate checks: html pages containing branded native audio/video controls; form elements not matched by owning page/style selectors; bare/global css selectors in local style bundles; hard coded z index hotspots; fixed/sticky declarations; missing viewport metadata; browser runtime x overflow; visible elements outside viewport; undersized interactive targets; default computed appearance signatures for form/media controls. first remediation reference social hub becomes the reference page because the user supplied live screenshots proving: native audio chrome inside messages; incomplete composer integration; fixed bottom geometry risk; mixed visual ownership. fix shared social hub components first so private messages and social pulse benefit together when they consume the same primitives.
